questions.subtopic: Lessor Classification — Direct Financing Test
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. leases equipment to Customer Inc. The lease does not meet any of the five criteria that would require classification as a sales-type lease. The equipment's fair value is $200,000 and its carrying amount is $160,000. The present value of the lease payments is $180,000, and an unrelated third party (not the lessee) guarantees a residual value with a present value of $30,000. Collection of the lease payments and the guaranteed residual amount is probable. How should Lessor Corp. classify the lease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sales-type lease, because the present value of the lease payments plus the residual value guarantee exceeds the fair value of the equipment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct financing lease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Operating lease, because none of the five sales-type classification criteria is met

choices.label: D
choices.text: Operating lease, because a residual value guarantee provided by a third party is excluded from the lessor's classification tests

questions.explanation: When none of the five sales-type criteria is met, the lessor applies a second test: the lease is a direct financing lease if (1) the present value of the lease payments plus the present value of any residual value guaranteed by the lessee OR by any other third party unrelated to the lessor equals or exceeds substantially all of the fair value of the underlying asset, and (2) collection is probable. Here $180,000 + $30,000 = $210,000, which exceeds the $200,000 fair value, and collection is probable, so the lease is a direct financing lease. The lease is not sales-type, because a third-party guarantee counts only in the direct financing test, never as a sales-type criterion; exceeding fair value does not convert the lease into a sales-type lease. Classifying the lease as operating is wrong because failing the five sales-type criteria is only the first step, and the third-party guarantee is specifically included in the direct financing test.
questions.explanationJa: 5つの販売型基準をいずれも満たさない場合、貸手は第2段階の判定を行う。(1) リース料の現在価値に、借手または貸手と無関係な第三者が保証した残存価値の現在価値を加えた額が、原資産の公正価値のほぼ全部以上であり、(2) 回収可能性が高い場合、直接金融型リースとなる。本問は $180,000 + $30,000 = $210,000 で公正価値 $200,000 を上回り、回収可能性も高いため直接金融型である。第三者保証は直接金融型テストにのみ算入され、販売型の判定基準にはならないため販売型ではない。また5基準を満たさないことは第1段階に過ぎず、第三者保証が直接金融型テストに含まれる以上、オペレーティングとするのは誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Lessor Classification — Commencement Near End of Economic Life
questions.stem: Lessor Corp. leases a machine to a customer on January 1, Year 1. The machine had a total economic life of 20 years when new and is now 16 years old, leaving 4 years of remaining economic life. The lease term is 4 years. The machine's fair value is $100,000 and the present value of the lease payments is $95,000. Ownership does not transfer at the end of the lease, there is no purchase option, and the machine is a standard model with an alternative use to Lessor Corp. Collection of the lease payments is probable. How should Lessor Corp. classify this lease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sales-type lease, because the 4-year lease term covers the entire remaining economic life of the machine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sales-type lease, because the present value of the lease payments is 95% of the machine's fair value

choices.label: C
choices.text: Operating lease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct financing lease, because the present value of the lease payments is substantially all of the fair value and collection is probable

questions.explanation: When the commencement date falls at or near the end of the underlying asset's economic life, the economic-life criterion and the present-value criterion are not used to classify the lease. A commencement date falling within the last 25% of the asset's total economic life is considered at or near the end of that life. The machine is 16 of 20 years old, so 80% of its life has elapsed and commencement falls in the final 25%. Both the 4-of-4-years economic life test and the 95% present value test ($95,000 of $100,000) are therefore disregarded. Of the remaining criteria, ownership does not transfer, there is no purchase option, and the asset is not specialized, so the lease is an operating lease. For the same reason the lease is not a direct financing lease, because that test also rests on the present value measure that is switched off here.
questions.explanationJa: リース開始日が原資産の経済的耐用年数の終わり近くに当たる場合、経済的耐用年数基準と現在価値基準は分類に用いない。経済的耐用年数の最後の25%以内に開始日がある場合が「終わり近く」に該当する。本問の機械は20年のうち16年が経過しており、耐用年数の80%が経過して最後の25%に入っている。したがって4年／残存4年という耐用年数テストも、$95,000 ÷ $100,000 = 95% という現在価値テストも適用しない。残る基準では、所有権移転なし、購入選択権なし、特殊仕様でもないため、オペレーティング・リースとなる。直接金融型テストも現在価値の指標に依存するため、同じ理由で適用されない。

questions.subtopic: Lessor Classification — Present Value Criterion
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. leases equipment with a fair value of $500,000 and a remaining economic life of 10 years. The lease term is 6 years and requires six annual payments of $95,000 due at the beginning of each year, the first payable on January 1, Year 1. Ownership does not transfer, there is no purchase option, and the equipment is not of a specialized nature. The rate implicit in the lease is 8%. The present value of an annuity due of $1 for 6 periods at 8% is 4.9927. Collection of the lease payments is probable. How should Lessor Corp. classify the lease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sales-type lease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct financing lease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Operating lease, because the 6-year lease term is only 60% of the equipment's remaining economic life

choices.label: D
choices.text: Operating lease, because the present value of the lease payments is less than the equipment's fair value

questions.explanation: The present value of the lease payments is $95,000 x 4.9927 = $474,307, which is 94.9% of the $500,000 fair value. That is substantially all of the fair value, so the present value criterion is met and the lease is a sales-type lease even though no other criterion is satisfied. Meeting any single one of the five criteria is sufficient. The 60% economic-life ratio is a separate criterion that fails, but a failed criterion does not override a criterion that is met. It is not a direct financing lease, because the direct financing test is applied only when none of the five sales-type criteria is met. The observation that $474,307 is less than $500,000 misstates the test, which compares the present value with substantially all of fair value, not with the entire fair value.
questions.explanationJa: リース料の現在価値は $95,000 × 4.9927 = $474,307 であり、公正価値 $500,000 の94.9%に相当する。これは公正価値のほぼ全部に当たるため現在価値基準を満たし、他の基準を満たさなくても販売型リースとなる。5基準のいずれか1つを満たせば販売型である。経済的耐用年数比率60%という別基準は満たさないが、満たさない基準があっても、満たした基準を打ち消すことはない。直接金融型テストは5基準のいずれも満たさない場合にのみ適用するため該当しない。また $474,307 < $500,000 という比較は基準の誤解で、テストは公正価値そのものではなく「ほぼ全部」との比較である。

questions.subtopic: Lessor Classification — The Five Criteria
questions.stem: Under ASC 842, which of the following facts, considered by itself, requires a lessor to classify a lease as a sales-type lease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The lease term is 60% of the remaining economic life of the underlying asset.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The lease grants the lessee an option to purchase the underlying asset that the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lessor is reasonably certain to collect the lease payments from the lessee.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lessee guarantees a residual value equal to 5% of the underlying asset's fair value.

questions.explanation: A purchase option that the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise is one of the five sales-type criteria, and meeting any one of them alone requires sales-type classification. A lease term equal to 60% of remaining economic life fails the major-part criterion, which is generally read as 75% or more. Probable collection of the lease payments is not a classification criterion at all; it is a condition applied after classification, affecting whether the lessor may recognize selling profit and derecognize the asset, and it is also one prong of the direct financing test. A small residual value guarantee of 5% of fair value adds very little to the present value of the lease payments and does not by itself cause the present value to reach substantially all of fair value.
questions.explanationJa: 借手が行使することがほぼ確実な購入選択権は販売型5基準の1つであり、いずれか1つを満たせば販売型に分類される。リース期間が残存経済的耐用年数の60%というのは「主要部分」基準（通常75%以上と解される）を満たさない。リース料の回収可能性が高いことは分類基準そのものではなく、分類後に適用される条件であり、販売益の認識と資産の認識中止の可否に影響するほか、直接金融型テストの一要件でもある。公正価値の5%という小額の残存価値保証は、リース料の現在価値をわずかに増やすだけで、それ自体では現在価値が公正価値のほぼ全部に達することにはならない。

questions.subtopic: Lessor Classification — Lease Term with Renewal Option
questions.stem: Lessor Corp. leases equipment with a remaining economic life of 8 years. The noncancellable period of the lease is 4 years, and the lessee holds an option to renew for an additional 3 years at a rate well below the expected market rate; at commencement the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise the renewal option. Ownership does not transfer, there is no purchase option, and the equipment is not specialized. Collection of the lease payments is probable. How should Lessor Corp. classify the lease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Operating lease, because the 4-year noncancellable period is only 50% of the remaining economic life of the equipment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Operating lease, because renewal options are excluded from the lease term unless ownership of the underlying asset transfers to the lessee

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct financing lease, because ownership of the equipment does not transfer to the lessee

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sales-type lease

questions.explanation: The lease term includes periods covered by a lessee renewal option when the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise it. A renewal rate well below market is a significant economic incentive that supports that conclusion, so the lease term is 4 + 3 = 7 years. Seven years is 87.5% of the 8-year remaining economic life, which is a major part of that life, so the lease is a sales-type lease. Stopping at the 4-year noncancellable period produces a 50% ratio and the wrong answer. Renewal options are not limited to leases that transfer ownership; the test is whether exercise is reasonably certain. The absence of a transfer of ownership does not make a lease direct financing, because the direct financing test applies only when none of the five sales-type criteria is met, and here the economic-life criterion is met.
questions.explanationJa: 借手が行使することがほぼ確実な更新選択権の対象期間は、リース期間に含める。市場水準を大きく下回る更新料率は重要な経済的インセンティブであり、その判断を裏付ける。したがってリース期間は 4 + 3 = 7年となる。7年は残存経済的耐用年数8年の87.5%であり主要部分に当たるため、販売型リースとなる。解約不能期間の4年で止めると50%となり誤った結論になる。更新選択権の算入は所有権移転を伴うリースに限られるものではなく、判定基準は行使がほぼ確実かどうかである。また所有権が移転しないことをもって直接金融型とするのは誤りで、直接金融型テストは5基準をいずれも満たさない場合にのみ適用され、本問では経済的耐用年数基準を満たしている。

questions.subtopic: Lessor Classification — Failing Both Tests
questions.stem: Lessor Corp. leases equipment with a fair value of $200,000 and a remaining economic life of 10 years. The lease term is 5 years. Ownership does not transfer, the lessee's purchase option is exercisable at the equipment's then-fair value, and the equipment is a standard model with an alternative use to Lessor Corp. The present value of the lease payments, which already includes the amount probable of being owed by the lessee under its residual value guarantee, is $165,000. No other party guarantees any residual value. Collection of the lease payments is probable. How should Lessor Corp. classify the lease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sales-type lease, because the 5-year lease term is half of the equipment's remaining economic life

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct financing lease, because the lessee's residual value guarantee is added to the lease payments and collection is probable

choices.label: C
choices.text: Operating lease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sales-type lease, because the present value of the lease payments exceeds 80% of the equipment's fair value

questions.explanation: None of the five sales-type criteria is met: ownership does not transfer, a purchase option priced at then-fair value is not one the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise, a 5-year term is 50% of the 10-year remaining economic life and is not a major part of it, the $165,000 present value is 82.5% of the $200,000 fair value and is not substantially all of it, and the equipment is not specialized. The direct financing test then fails as well, because the lessee's guarantee is already inside the $165,000 and no third party guarantees any residual, so there is nothing further to add to reach substantially all of fair value. The lease is therefore an operating lease. An 80% threshold is not the standard; the present value test looks for substantially all of fair value, generally read as 90% or more.
questions.explanationJa: 販売型の5基準はいずれも満たさない。所有権は移転せず、行使価格が行使時点の公正価値である購入選択権は行使がほぼ確実とはいえず、5年は残存経済的耐用年数10年の50%で主要部分に当たらず、現在価値 $165,000 は公正価値 $200,000 の82.5%でほぼ全部とはいえず、設備も特殊仕様ではない。次に直接金融型テストも満たさない。借手の残存価値保証は既に $165,000 に含まれており、第三者による保証もないため、公正価値のほぼ全部に届かせる追加項目が存在しないからである。したがってオペレーティング・リースとなる。なお80%という閾値は基準に存在せず、現在価値テストは公正価値のほぼ全部（通常90%以上と解される）を求めている。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Net Investment at Commencement
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp., a manufacturer, leases equipment to a customer under a lease properly classified as a sales-type lease. The lease term is 5 years and requires five annual payments of $100,000 due at the beginning of each year, the first received on January 1, Year 1. At the end of the lease the equipment reverts to Lessor Corp., which estimates its residual value at that date will be $50,000; no part of the residual value is guaranteed by any party. The rate implicit in the lease is 8%. The present value of an annuity due of $1 for 5 periods at 8% is 4.3121, and the present value of $1 in 5 periods at 8% is 0.6806. What amount should Lessor Corp. report as its net investment in the lease at January 1, Year 1?
questions.explanation: A lessor's net investment in a sales-type lease equals the lease receivable plus the unguaranteed residual asset, both measured at present value using the rate implicit in the lease. The lease receivable is $100,000 x 4.3121 = $431,210. The unguaranteed residual asset is $50,000 x 0.6806 = $34,030. The net investment is $431,210 + $34,030 = $465,240. The $431,210 amount omits the residual asset entirely, but an unguaranteed residual is still part of the net investment because the lessor expects to recover it by taking back the equipment. The $481,210 amount adds the $50,000 residual without discounting it back 5 years. The $433,300 amount discounts the payments with an ordinary annuity factor of 3.9927, which is wrong because the first payment is received at commencement and is not discounted at all.
questions.explanationJa: 販売型リースにおける貸手の正味リース投資未回収額は、リース債権と無保証残存資産の合計であり、いずれもリースの計算利子率で割り引いた現在価値で測定する。リース債権は $100,000 × 4.3121 = $431,210。無保証残存資産は $50,000 × 0.6806 = $34,030。正味投資額は $431,210 + $34,030 = $465,240 となる。$431,210 は残存資産を完全に除外しているが、無保証であっても貸手は設備の返還により回収を見込むため正味投資額に含まれる。$481,210 は残存価値 $50,000 を5年分割り引かずに加算している。$433,300 は普通年金現価係数 3.9927 を用いているが、初回支払はリース開始時に受領し割引の対象外であるため誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Lessee-Guaranteed Residual in Lease Payments
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. leases equipment under a sales-type lease with a 4-year term. The lease requires four annual payments of $60,000 due at the end of each year. The lessee guarantees that the equipment will be worth $30,000 when it is returned at the end of the lease term. Lessor Corp. estimates the equipment will actually be worth $22,000 at that date, so the lessee is expected to owe $8,000 under the guarantee. The rate implicit in the lease is 10%. The present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 for 4 periods at 10% is 3.1699, and the present value of $1 in 4 periods at 10% is 0.6830. What is Lessor Corp.'s net investment in the lease at January 1, Year 1?
questions.explanation: A lessor measures its lease receivable using the full amount of the residual value guaranteed by the lessee, because it expects to derive that entire amount either from the returned equipment or from the lessee under the guarantee. The limitation to the amount probable of being owed applies only to a lessee measuring its own lease liability. The receivable is $60,000 x 3.1699 = $190,194 plus $30,000 x 0.6830 = $20,490, for a net investment of $210,684. The $195,658 amount discounts only the $8,000 expected shortfall, which is the lessee's measurement rule applied to the wrong party. The $205,220 amount discounts only the $22,000 expected value of the equipment and ignores that the guarantee lifts the lessor's expected recovery to $30,000. The $190,194 amount omits the residual value entirely.
questions.explanationJa: 貸手はリース債権の測定にあたり、借手が保証した残存価値の全額を用いる。返還される設備からか、保証に基づく借手からの支払によるかを問わず、その全額の回収を見込んでいるためである。「支払う可能性が高い金額」に限定する規定は、借手が自らのリース負債を測定する場合にのみ適用される。債権は $60,000 × 3.1699 = $190,194 に $30,000 × 0.6830 = $20,490 を加えた $210,684 となる。$195,658 は不足見込額 $8,000 のみを割り引いており、借手側の測定ルールを貸手に誤って適用している。$205,220 は設備の見積価値 $22,000 のみを割り引いており、保証によって貸手の回収見込額が $30,000 に引き上げられる点を無視している。$190,194 は残存価値を全く含めていない。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Total Year 1 Income
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp., a dealer, leases equipment to a customer under a sales-type lease. The lease requires five annual payments of $100,000 due at the end of each year. There is no residual value. The rate implicit in the lease is 10%, and the present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 for 5 periods at 10% is 3.7908. The equipment's carrying amount in Lessor Corp.'s inventory is $300,000. Collection of the lease payments is probable and Lessor Corp. incurred no initial direct costs. What total amount should Lessor Corp. recognize in Year 1 income from this lease?
questions.explanation: A dealer lessor recognizes selling profit at commencement plus interest income over the lease term. The net investment is $100,000 x 3.7908 = $379,080, so selling profit is $379,080 - $300,000 = $79,080. Interest income for Year 1 is $379,080 x 10% = $37,908, because the payments are due at the end of each year and the full net investment is outstanding for all of Year 1. Total Year 1 income is $79,080 + $37,908 = $116,988. The $79,080 amount captures only the day-one profit and ignores interest. The $37,908 amount captures only interest and ignores the selling profit that a dealer recognizes at commencement. The $106,988 amount reduces the net investment by a $100,000 payment before computing interest, which would be correct only if the first payment were received at commencement.
questions.explanationJa: ディーラーである貸手は、リース開始時に販売益を認識し、その後リース期間にわたり受取利息を認識する。正味リース投資未回収額は $100,000 × 3.7908 = $379,080 であり、販売益は $379,080 − $300,000 = $79,080 となる。支払は各年度末であるため正味投資額は Year 1 を通じて全額が未回収であり、Year 1 の受取利息は $379,080 × 10% = $37,908。Year 1 の合計は $79,080 + $37,908 = $116,988 である。$79,080 は初日の販売益のみで受取利息を無視している。$37,908 は受取利息のみで、ディーラーがリース開始時に認識する販売益を無視している。$106,988 は利息計算の前に $100,000 の支払を差し引いており、これは初回支払をリース開始時に受領する場合にのみ正しい。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Net Investment After Two Years
questions.stem: Lessor Corp.'s net investment in a sales-type lease was $500,000 at the commencement date of January 1, Year 1. The lease requires five annual payments of $120,000 due at the end of each year, and the equipment reverts to Lessor Corp. at the end of the lease with an unguaranteed residual value. The rate implicit in the lease is 8%. Lessor Corp. has not revised any of its estimates. What is the carrying amount of the net investment in the lease at December 31, Year 2?
questions.explanation: The net investment is accreted using the effective interest method: each year interest is added at the rate implicit in the lease and the cash received is deducted. Year 1 interest is $500,000 x 8% = $40,000, so the balance at December 31, Year 1 is $500,000 + $40,000 - $120,000 = $420,000. Year 2 interest is $420,000 x 8% = $33,600, so the balance at December 31, Year 2 is $420,000 + $33,600 - $120,000 = $333,600. The $420,000 amount is the balance one year too early. The $260,000 amount simply deducts two $120,000 payments and ignores interest accretion entirely. The $340,000 amount accretes interest at $40,000 in both years instead of recomputing it on the reduced balance.
questions.explanationJa: 正味リース投資未回収額は実効金利法で増価する。毎期、計算利子率による利息を加算し、受領したキャッシュを控除する。Year 1 の利息は $500,000 × 8% = $40,000 であり、Year 1 末残高は $500,000 + $40,000 − $120,000 = $420,000。Year 2 の利息は $420,000 × 8% = $33,600 であり、Year 2 末残高は $420,000 + $33,600 − $120,000 = $333,600 となる。$420,000 は1年前の残高である。$260,000 は $120,000 の支払を2回控除しただけで利息の増価を全く考慮していない。$340,000 は減少後の残高で計算し直さず、両年とも $40,000 の利息を加算している。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Total Interest Income Over the Term
questions.stem: At the commencement of a sales-type lease, Lessor Corp. recorded a net investment in the lease of $300,000. The lease requires six annual payments of $58,000 due at the end of each year. At the end of the lease term the equipment reverts to Lessor Corp., which expects to realize its estimated unguaranteed residual value of $25,000 at that date. Assuming all payments are received as scheduled and the residual value is realized exactly as estimated, what total amount of interest income will Lessor Corp. recognize over the lease term?
questions.explanation: After commencement, all of a lessor's income from a sales-type lease is interest income earned by accreting the net investment. Total interest income equals everything the lessor expects to receive less the amount recorded as the net investment. The lessor expects six payments of $58,000, or $348,000, plus the $25,000 residual value realized on the returned equipment, for a total of $373,000. Interest income is $373,000 - $300,000 = $73,000. The $48,000 amount excludes the residual value from the expected recoveries even though the residual asset is part of the $300,000 net investment being accreted. The $98,000 amount subtracts the residual value from the net investment as well as adding it to the recoveries, double counting it. The $25,000 amount is the residual value itself, not interest.
questions.explanationJa: リース開始後、販売型リースから貸手が得る収益はすべて、正味リース投資未回収額の増価による受取利息である。総受取利息は、貸手が受け取ると見込む総額から、正味投資額として計上した金額を差し引いた額に等しい。貸手は $58,000 の支払を6回、すなわち $348,000 と、返還された設備で実現する残存価値 $25,000 を見込むため、合計 $373,000 である。受取利息は $373,000 − $300,000 = $73,000 となる。$48,000 は回収見込額から残存価値を除いているが、残存資産は増価の対象である $300,000 の正味投資額に含まれている。$98,000 は残存価値を回収見込額に加えつつ正味投資額からも控除しており、二重計上である。$25,000 は残存価値そのもので、利息ではない。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Purchase Option in Lease Payments
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. leases equipment under a sales-type lease with a 4-year term. The lease requires four annual payments of $50,000 due at the beginning of each year, the first received on January 1, Year 1. The lessee holds an option to purchase the equipment for $40,000 at the end of Year 4, and at commencement the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise the option. The rate implicit in the lease is 8%. The present value of an annuity due of $1 for 4 periods at 8% is 3.5771, the present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 for 4 periods at 8% is 3.3121, and the present value of $1 in 4 periods at 8% is 0.7350. What amount should Lessor Corp. record as its net investment in the lease at commencement?
questions.explanation: The exercise price of a purchase option that the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise is included in the lease payments, and it is discounted from the date the option would be exercised. The four annual payments give $50,000 x 3.5771 = $178,855, and the option price gives $40,000 x 0.7350 = $29,400, for a net investment of $208,255. There is no separate residual asset, because the lessor expects the equipment to be purchased rather than returned. The $178,855 amount omits the option price, which is wrong once exercise is reasonably certain. The $218,855 amount adds the $40,000 option price without discounting it 4 years. The $195,005 amount discounts the annual payments with the ordinary annuity factor of 3.3121, even though the first payment is received at commencement and is not discounted.
questions.explanationJa: 借手が行使することがほぼ確実な購入選択権の行使価格はリース料に含め、行使予定日から割り引く。年次支払は $50,000 × 3.5771 = $178,855、行使価格は $40,000 × 0.7350 = $29,400 で、正味リース投資未回収額は $208,255 となる。貸手は設備が返還されず購入されると見込むため、別途の残存資産は生じない。$178,855 は行使価格を除外しているが、行使がほぼ確実である以上これは誤りである。$218,855 は行使価格 $40,000 を4年分割り引かずに加算している。$195,005 は普通年金現価係数 3.3121 で年次支払を割り引いているが、初回支払はリース開始時に受領し割引の対象外である。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Commencement Journal Entry
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp., a manufacturer, delivers equipment from its inventory to a customer under a lease properly classified as a sales-type lease. The net investment in the lease is $700,000, the equipment's carrying amount in inventory is $520,000, and collection of the lease payments is probable. Lessor Corp. presents revenue and cost of goods sold gross because it uses leases as an alternative means of realizing value from the goods it makes. Which of the following describes the entry Lessor Corp. records at the commencement date?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Debit net investment in the lease $700,000 and credit sales revenue $700,000; debit cost of goods sold $520,000 and credit inventory $520,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: Debit net investment in the lease $700,000, credit inventory $520,000, and credit deferred gross profit $180,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: Debit net investment in the lease $520,000 and credit inventory $520,000, with the $180,000 difference recognized over the lease term as additional interest income

choices.label: D
choices.text: Debit net investment in the lease $700,000 and credit inventory $700,000, with no gain or loss recognized at the commencement date

questions.explanation: In a sales-type lease for which collection is probable, the lessor derecognizes the underlying asset, records the net investment in the lease, and recognizes the selling profit immediately. Presenting the transaction gross means recording sales revenue of $700,000 against the net investment and cost of goods sold of $520,000 against inventory, producing $180,000 of day-one profit. Deferring the $180,000 as deferred gross profit, or building it into interest income over the term, describes the treatment of selling profit in a direct financing lease, not a sales-type lease. Recording the net investment at the $520,000 carrying amount understates the receivable, which must be measured at the present value of the lease payments and residual, and crediting inventory for the full $700,000 would remove more from inventory than the asset ever cost.
questions.explanationJa: 回収可能性が高い販売型リースでは、貸手は原資産の認識を中止し、正味リース投資未回収額を計上するとともに販売益を即時に認識する。総額表示では、正味投資額に対して売上高 $700,000 を、棚卸資産に対して売上原価 $520,000 を計上し、初日の利益 $180,000 が生じる。$180,000 を繰延売上総利益として繰り延べたり、リース期間にわたり受取利息に織り込んだりするのは、販売型ではなく直接金融型リースにおける販売益の処理である。正味投資額を帳簿価額 $520,000 で計上すると債権が過少となる。債権はリース料と残存価値の現在価値で測定しなければならない。また棚卸資産を $700,000 で貸方計上すると、取得原価を超える金額を棚卸資産から除去することになる。

questions.subtopic: Operating Lease — Straight-Line Income with Partial First Year
questions.stem: On October 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. leases office space to a tenant under a 5-year operating lease. As an inducement, the first 6 months of the lease are rent free. Beginning April 1, Year 2, the tenant must pay $11,000 per month for the remaining 54 months of the lease term. There are no other payments, and Lessor Corp. incurred no initial direct costs. What amount of lease income should Lessor Corp. recognize for the year ended December 31, Year 1?
questions.explanation: A lessor recognizes operating lease income on a straight-line basis over the lease term, including any rent-free period. Total lease payments are 54 months x $11,000 = $594,000 over a 60-month term, so monthly income is $594,000 / 60 = $9,900. The lease commenced October 1, Year 1, so only 3 months fall in Year 1: 3 x $9,900 = $29,700. Recognizing nothing follows the cash rent rather than the straight-line pattern, and the whole point of straight-lining is that a rent-free period does not mean a period without income. The $33,000 amount applies the $11,000 contractual rate to 3 months even though no rent is contractually due in Year 1. The $118,800 amount recognizes a full 12 months of straight-line income in a year in which the lease ran for only 3 months.
questions.explanationJa: 貸手はオペレーティング・リース収益を、フリーレント期間も含むリース期間にわたり定額で認識する。総リース料は 54か月 × $11,000 = $594,000、リース期間は60か月であるため、月額収益は $594,000 ÷ 60 = $9,900 となる。リース開始日は Year 1 の10月1日であり Year 1 に属するのは3か月分のみなので、3 × $9,900 = $29,700。$0 は定額法ではなく現金賃料に従った結果であり、フリーレント期間でも収益が生じるというのが定額計上の要点である。$33,000 は Year 1 に契約上の賃料が発生していないにもかかわらず、契約月額 $11,000 を3か月に適用している。$118,800 はリースが3か月しか進行していない年度に、12か月分の定額収益を計上している。

questions.subtopic: Lessor — Definition of Initial Direct Costs
questions.stem:
Lessor Corp. incurred the following costs in connection with negotiating and executing a new 6-year operating lease:
Sales commissions payable only if the lease is executed | $18,000
External legal fees for negotiating and drafting the lease agreement | $12,000
Allocated salaries of Lessor Corp.'s in-house leasing department | $25,000
Advertising to attract prospective tenants | $6,000
What amount qualifies as initial direct costs under ASC 842?
questions.explanation: Initial direct costs are limited to incremental costs of obtaining a lease that would not have been incurred if the lease had not been obtained. A commission payable only if the lease is executed meets that definition, so $18,000 qualifies. External legal fees for negotiating and drafting are incurred whether or not the lease is ultimately executed, so they are expensed as incurred, and the $30,000 total that adds them to the commission is therefore too high. Allocated in-house salaries are costs the entity incurs regardless of any particular lease, which is why the $43,000 total is wrong. Advertising is a general cost of finding tenants and not a cost of obtaining any specific lease, so the $61,000 total that sweeps in every cost listed overstates the amount.
questions.explanationJa: 当初直接費用は、そのリースを獲得しなければ発生しなかった増分費用に限定される。リースが締結された場合にのみ支払う手数料はこの定義を満たすため、$18,000 が該当する。交渉・契約書作成に係る外部弁護士費用は最終的に締結されるか否かにかかわらず発生するため発生時に費用処理され、これを手数料に加えた $30,000 は過大である。社内部門の配賦給与は特定のリースの有無にかかわらず発生する費用であり、$43,000 が誤りとなる理由である。広告費はテナントを探す一般的な費用で、特定のリース獲得費用ではないため、列挙された費用をすべて合算した $61,000 は金額を過大に計上している。

questions.subtopic: Operating Lease — Variable Lease Payments
questions.stem: Lessor Corp. leases retail space to a tenant under a 5-year operating lease. The lease requires fixed annual rent of $200,000 plus contingent rent equal to 4% of the tenant's annual sales in excess of $3,000,000. The tenant's sales were $2,800,000 in Year 1, $3,200,000 in Year 2, and $4,500,000 in Year 3. What amount of lease income should Lessor Corp. recognize in Year 3?
questions.explanation: Variable lease payments that depend on sales are excluded from the fixed lease payments that are recognized on a straight-line basis, and are instead recognized as income in the period in which the changes in facts and circumstances on which they are based occur. The fixed rent is a level $200,000 per year, and the Year 3 contingent rent is 4% x ($4,500,000 - $3,000,000) = $60,000, so Year 3 lease income is $260,000. Recognizing only $200,000 ignores contingent rent that has actually been earned. The $380,000 amount applies the 4% rate to all $4,500,000 of sales instead of only the excess over the $3,000,000 threshold. The $212,000 amount spreads the $60,000 of contingent rent over the 5-year term, which is the treatment for fixed escalating rents, not for sales-based variable payments.
questions.explanationJa: 売上高に連動する変動リース料は、定額で認識する固定リース料から除外し、その算定根拠となる事実・状況の変化が生じた期間の収益として認識する。固定賃料は毎年一定の $200,000 であり、Year 3 の歩合賃料は 4% × ($4,500,000 − $3,000,000) = $60,000 であるから、Year 3 のリース収益は $260,000 となる。$200,000 のみの計上は、実際に獲得した歩合賃料を無視している。$380,000 は基準額 $3,000,000 の超過分ではなく売上高 $4,500,000 の全額に4%を乗じている。$212,000 は歩合賃料 $60,000 を5年のリース期間に配分しているが、これは固定の逓増賃料に対する処理であり、売上高連動の変動リース料には当てはまらない。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Year 2 Interest Income
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. enters into a sales-type lease requiring four annual payments of $100,000 due at the end of each year. There is no residual value. The rate implicit in the lease is 10%, and the present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 for 4 periods at 10% is 3.1699. What amount of interest income should Lessor Corp. recognize in Year 2?
questions.explanation: The net investment at commencement is $100,000 x 3.1699 = $316,990. Year 1 interest income is $316,990 x 10% = $31,699, and the December 31, Year 1 payment of $100,000 reduces the balance to $316,990 + $31,699 - $100,000 = $248,689. Year 2 interest income is $248,689 x 10% = $24,869. The $31,699 amount is the Year 1 figure, which overstates Year 2 because the balance has declined. The $21,699 amount deducts the first payment from the original $316,990 without first adding the interest that accrued during Year 1. The $20,753 amount divides total interest of $400,000 - $316,990 = $83,010 evenly over 4 years, but interest income follows the effective interest method rather than a straight-line pattern.
questions.explanationJa: リース開始時の正味リース投資未回収額は $100,000 × 3.1699 = $316,990 である。Year 1 の受取利息は $316,990 × 10% = $31,699 であり、Year 1 末の支払 $100,000 により残高は $316,990 + $31,699 − $100,000 = $248,689 となる。Year 2 の受取利息は $248,689 × 10% = $24,869。$31,699 は Year 1 の金額であり、残高が減少しているため Year 2 としては過大である。$21,699 は Year 1 中に発生した利息を加算せずに、当初の $316,990 から初回支払を控除している。$20,753 は総利息 $400,000 − $316,990 = $83,010 を4年で均等配分しているが、受取利息は定額法ではなく実効金利法に従う。

questions.subtopic: Sales-Type Lease — Total Income Over the Lease Term
questions.stem: Lessor Corp. enters into a 5-year sales-type lease for equipment that cost Lessor Corp. $340,000. The lease requires five annual payments of $90,000 due at the end of each year. At the end of the lease term the equipment reverts to Lessor Corp., which expects it to be worth $30,000 at that date; no party guarantees the residual value. Assuming all payments are collected and the residual value is realized exactly as expected, what total amount of income will Lessor Corp. recognize from this lease over the entire lease term?
questions.explanation: Over the full term, the lessor's total income equals everything it realizes from the arrangement less the cost of the equipment given up, regardless of how that income is split between selling profit at commencement and interest income later. Total realizations are five payments of $90,000, or $450,000, plus the $30,000 residual value realized when the equipment comes back, for $480,000. Total income is $480,000 - $340,000 = $140,000. The $110,000 amount ignores the residual value the lessor actually recovers. The $170,000 amount subtracts the residual value from the equipment's cost and also adds it to the realizations, counting it twice. The $80,000 amount deducts the residual value from the payments instead of adding it.
questions.explanationJa: リース期間全体を通じた貸手の総収益は、取決めから実現する総額から手放した設備の原価を差し引いた額に等しく、それがリース開始時の販売益と事後の受取利息にどう配分されるかは影響しない。実現総額は $90,000 の支払5回分 $450,000 に、設備返還時に実現する残存価値 $30,000 を加えた $480,000 である。総収益は $480,000 − $340,000 = $140,000 となる。$110,000 は貸手が実際に回収する残存価値を無視している。$170,000 は残存価値を実現額に加えつつ設備原価からも控除しており、二重に数えている。$80,000 は残存価値を加算せず支払額から控除している。

questions.subtopic: Direct Financing Lease — Initial Direct Costs
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Lessor Corp. enters into a lease properly classified as a direct financing lease. Before considering initial direct costs, the present value of the lease payments plus the present value of the guaranteed residual value, discounted at the rate implicit in the lease, is $400,000, which equals the fair value of the equipment. The equipment's carrying amount on Lessor Corp.'s books is also $400,000. Lessor Corp. pays a $12,000 commission that qualifies as an initial direct cost. At what amount should Lessor Corp. report its net investment in the lease at commencement, and how are the initial direct costs recognized?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $400,000; the $12,000 is expensed at the commencement date

choices.label: B
choices.text: $388,000; the $12,000 reduces the net investment and is recognized as additional interest income over the lease term

choices.label: C
choices.text: $412,000; the $12,000 is included in the net investment and is recognized over the lease term through a lower effective interest rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: $412,000; the $12,000 is amortized on a straight-line basis over the lease term as a separate deferred asset

questions.explanation: In a direct financing lease there is no selling profit to recognize at commencement, so initial direct costs are deferred rather than expensed. They are added to the net investment in the lease, giving $400,000 + $12,000 = $412,000, and the rate implicit in the lease is redetermined so that the higher carrying amount is recovered over the term. The effect is a lower effective rate and therefore less interest income each period, which is how the cost is recognized. Expensing the $12,000 immediately is the treatment required for a sales-type lease in which the lessor recognizes selling profit. Reducing the net investment to $388,000 moves the cost in the wrong direction, since a cost incurred increases the amount the lessor must recover. The costs are part of the net investment and are not carried as a separate asset amortized straight line.
questions.explanationJa: 直接金融型リースではリース開始時に認識する販売益が存在しないため、当初直接費用は費用処理せず繰り延べる。当初直接費用は正味リース投資未回収額に加算され $400,000 + $12,000 = $412,000 となり、増加した帳簿価額をリース期間にわたり回収するよう計算利子率を再決定する。その結果、実効利率が低下し各期の受取利息が減少することで費用が認識される。$12,000 を即時に費用処理するのは、貸手が販売益を認識する販売型リースに求められる処理である。正味投資額を $388,000 に減額するのは向きが逆で、支出した費用は貸手が回収すべき金額を増加させる。また当初直接費用は正味投資額の一部であり、別個の資産として定額償却するものではない。

questions.subtopic: Residual Value — Other-Than-Temporary Decline
questions.stem: At the commencement of a sales-type lease, Lessor Corp. recorded an unguaranteed residual asset of $18,000, representing the present value of an estimated $30,000 residual value. By December 31, Year 2, accretion has increased the carrying amount of the residual asset to $21,000. At that date Lessor Corp. determines that the expected residual value has declined from $30,000 to $16,000 and that the decline is other than temporary. The present value of the revised $16,000 estimate at December 31, Year 2 is $11,200. What amount of loss should Lessor Corp. recognize at December 31, Year 2?

choices.label: C
choices.text: No loss is recognized; the revised estimate is applied prospectively over the remaining lease term.

questions.explanation: When the estimated residual value of the underlying asset declines and the decline is other than temporary, the lessor revises the estimate and recognizes the resulting reduction in its net investment as a loss in the period of the decline. The residual asset is carried at $21,000 and must be written down to the present value of the revised estimate, $11,200, producing a loss of $21,000 - $11,200 = $9,800. The $14,000 amount is the undiscounted decline from $30,000 to $16,000, which ignores that the residual asset is carried at present value. The $6,800 amount measures the write-down from the original $18,000 recorded at commencement instead of from the accreted $21,000 carrying amount. Applying the change prospectively is the treatment for a change in estimate that is not an other-than-temporary decline in residual value.
questions.explanationJa: 原資産の見積残存価値が低下し、その低下が一時的でない場合、貸手は見積りを修正し、正味リース投資未回収額の減少額をその低下が生じた期間の損失として認識する。残存資産の帳簿価額は $21,000 であり、修正後見積りの現在価値 $11,200 まで切り下げる必要があるため、損失は $21,000 − $11,200 = $9,800 となる。$14,000 は $30,000 から $16,000 への割引前の減少額であり、残存資産が現在価値で計上されている点を無視している。$6,800 は増価後の帳簿価額 $21,000 ではなく、リース開始時に計上した当初の $18,000 からの切下げ額を測定している。将来に向かって処理するのは、残存価値の一時的でない低下に該当しない見積りの変更に対する扱いである。

questions.subtopic: Residual Value — Upward Revision
questions.stem: At the end of Year 3 of a 6-year direct financing lease, Lessor Corp. determines that the estimated residual value of the underlying asset at the end of the lease term has increased from $40,000 to $55,000 because of unexpectedly strong demand in the used equipment market. How should Lessor Corp. account for this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No adjustment is made; upward revisions of the estimated residual value are not recognized.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recognize a $15,000 gain in Year 3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the net investment in the lease by the present value of the $15,000 increase and credit a deferred gain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the net investment in the lease by the present value of the $15,000 increase and recognize the effect prospectively as additional interest income over the remaining lease term.

questions.explanation: The residual value estimate is reviewed for declines, not increases. An other-than-temporary decline requires an immediate loss, but an upward adjustment to the estimated residual value is not recognized at all. The benefit of a higher residual value is realized only when the asset is eventually sold or re-leased after the lease term ends. Recognizing a $15,000 gain therefore anticipates income that has not been realized, and both approaches that write up the net investment accomplish the same anticipation, whether the credit is parked in a deferred gain account or spread through interest income over the remaining term.
questions.explanationJa: 残存価値の見積りは、上昇ではなく低下について見直す。一時的でない低下には即時の損失計上が必要だが、見積残存価値の上方修正は一切認識しない。残存価値が高まったことの便益は、リース期間終了後に資産を売却または再リースした時点で初めて実現する。したがって $15,000 の利益を計上するのは未実現の収益を先取りするものであり、正味リース投資未回収額を増額する2つの方法も、貸方を繰延利益に置くか残存期間の受取利息に配分するかの違いはあれ、同じ先取りを行っている点で誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Residual Value — Guaranteed and Unguaranteed Portions
questions.stem: Lessor Corp. enters into a 5-year sales-type lease. The equipment is estimated to be worth $60,000 when it reverts to Lessor Corp. at the end of the lease term, and the lessee guarantees $45,000 of that amount. The rate implicit in the lease is 8%, and the present value of $1 in 5 periods at 8% is 0.6806. What total amount relating to the residual value is included in Lessor Corp.'s net investment in the lease at the commencement date?
questions.explanation: A lessor's net investment includes the entire estimated residual value at present value. The guaranteed portion is part of the lease receivable and the unguaranteed portion is recorded as the unguaranteed residual asset, but both are measured at present value using the rate implicit in the lease, so the total included is $60,000 x 0.6806 = $40,836. The $30,627 amount discounts only the $45,000 guaranteed portion and drops the unguaranteed residual asset, which the lessor still expects to recover by taking back the equipment. The $10,209 amount discounts only the $15,000 unguaranteed portion and drops the guaranteed receivable. The $60,000 amount fails to discount the residual value back the 5 years until it will be recovered.
questions.explanationJa: 貸手の正味リース投資未回収額には、見積残存価値の全額を現在価値で含める。保証部分はリース債権の一部となり、無保証部分は無保証残存資産として計上されるが、いずれもリースの計算利子率で割り引いた現在価値で測定するため、含まれる合計額は $60,000 × 0.6806 = $40,836 となる。$30,627 は保証部分 $45,000 のみを割り引き、貸手が設備の返還により回収を見込む無保証残存資産を除外している。$10,209 は無保証部分 $15,000 のみを割り引き、保証部分の債権を除外している。$60,000 は回収までの5年分の割引を行っていない。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — When the Transfer Fails to Be a Sale
questions.stem: Under ASC 842, which of the following facts would cause the transfer of an asset in a sale-leaseback transaction to fail to qualify as a sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sale price of the asset differs from its fair value at the transfer date.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The seller-lessee is the buyer-lessor's largest customer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The leaseback is classified as a finance lease by the seller-lessee.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The leaseback term is 30% of the asset's remaining economic life.

questions.explanation: A transfer in a sale-leaseback is not a sale if the leaseback would be classified as a finance lease by the seller-lessee or as a sales-type lease by the buyer-lessor, because that classification shows the seller-lessee never gave up control of the asset. A difference between the sale price and fair value does not defeat sale accounting; it is corrected by adjusting the transaction, with a shortfall treated as prepaid rent and an excess treated as additional financing. A customer relationship between the parties is not a criterion. A leaseback covering 30% of remaining economic life is a short leaseback that is consistent with an operating classification and with a genuine transfer of control.
questions.explanationJa: セール&リースバックにおける資産の移転は、リースバックが売主借手にとってファイナンス・リースに、または買主貸手にとって販売型リースに分類される場合には売却とならない。その分類は、売主借手が資産の支配を手放していないことを示すからである。売却価格と公正価値の差異は売却処理を否定しない。取引の調整により是正され、不足額は前払賃料、超過額は追加の金融として扱われる。両当事者間の取引関係は判定基準ではない。残存経済的耐用年数の30%というリースバック期間は短期であり、オペレーティング分類とも真の支配移転とも整合する。

questions.subtopic: Failed Sale-Leaseback — Financial Liability Balance
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Seller-Lessee Corp. transfers a building with a carrying amount of $1,800,000 to Buyer-Lessor Corp. for $2,500,000 cash and leases it back for 15 years. Because Seller-Lessee Corp. holds a substantive option to repurchase the building at a fixed price, the transfer does not qualify as a sale under ASC 606. The leaseback requires annual payments of $220,000 due at the end of each year, and the imputed interest rate on the financing is 7%. What is the carrying amount of the financial liability at December 31, Year 1?
questions.explanation: When the transfer fails to qualify as a sale, the seller-lessee keeps the building on its books and records the cash received as a financial liability accounted for under the interest method. Year 1 interest is $2,500,000 x 7% = $175,000, and the $220,000 payment covers that interest and reduces principal by $45,000, so the liability at December 31, Year 1 is $2,500,000 + $175,000 - $220,000 = $2,455,000. The $2,280,000 amount applies the payment entirely to principal and ignores interest. The $2,675,000 amount accrues interest but never applies the payment. The $2,500,000 amount leaves the liability unchanged, which would be correct only if the annual payment exactly equaled the interest accrued.
questions.explanationJa: 移転が売却の要件を満たさない場合、売主借手は建物を自らの帳簿に残したまま、受領した現金を金融負債として計上し、利息法で処理する。Year 1 の利息は $2,500,000 × 7% = $175,000 であり、$220,000 の支払はこの利息を賄ったうえで元本を $45,000 減少させるため、Year 1 末の負債は $2,500,000 + $175,000 − $220,000 = $2,455,000 となる。$2,280,000 は支払全額を元本に充当し利息を無視している。$2,675,000 は利息を計上しながら支払を反映していない。$2,500,000 は負債を変動させていないが、これは年間支払額が発生利息とちょうど一致する場合にのみ正しい。

questions.subtopic: Failed Sale-Leaseback — Buyer-Lessor Accounting
questions.stem: Buyer-Lessor Corp. pays $2,500,000 to Seller-Lessee Corp. for a building and immediately leases the building back to Seller-Lessee Corp. Because of a substantive repurchase option held by Seller-Lessee Corp., the transfer does not qualify as a sale under ASC 606. How should Buyer-Lessor Corp. account for the transaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recognize the building at $2,500,000 and account for the leaseback as an operating lease.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recognize a financial asset of $2,500,000, accounted for under the interest method, and do not recognize the building.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recognize the building at Seller-Lessee Corp.'s carrying amount and recognize the excess paid as goodwill.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recognize the building at $2,500,000 and a net investment in the lease equal to the present value of the leaseback payments.

questions.explanation: A failed sale-leaseback is accounted for as a financing by both parties. The buyer-lessor has not obtained control of the building, so it does not recognize the asset; instead it recognizes a financial asset of $2,500,000 and accretes interest income as the leaseback payments are received. Recognizing the building and an operating lease is the accounting for a transfer that does qualify as a sale. Recording the building at the transferor's carrying amount with goodwill for the difference has no basis, because this is neither an asset acquisition measured that way nor a business combination. Recognizing both the building and a net investment in the lease double counts the same economic interest, since a net investment arises only when the asset has been derecognized.
questions.explanationJa: 売却要件を満たさないセール&リースバックは、両当事者において金融取引として処理する。買主貸手は建物の支配を獲得していないため資産を認識せず、代わりに $2,500,000 の金融資産を認識し、リースバック料の受領に応じて受取利息を増価させる。建物とオペレーティング・リースを認識するのは、売却要件を満たす移転に対する処理である。建物を譲渡人の帳簿価額で計上し差額をのれんとするのは根拠がない。そのように測定される資産取得でも企業結合でもないからである。建物と正味リース投資未回収額の双方を認識するのは同一の経済的持分を二重に計上するもので、正味投資額は資産の認識を中止した場合にのみ生じる。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — Gain and Right-of-Use Asset
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Seller-Lessee Corp. sells a warehouse with a carrying amount of $2,100,000 to Buyer-Lessor Corp. for $3,000,000 cash, which equals the warehouse's fair value. The warehouse has a remaining economic life of 30 years. Seller-Lessee Corp. immediately leases the warehouse back for 5 years at $250,000 per year payable at the beginning of each year, with no renewal or purchase option. The transfer qualifies as a sale under ASC 606 and the leaseback is classified as an operating lease. Seller-Lessee Corp.'s incremental borrowing rate is 6%, and the present value of an annuity due of $1 for 5 periods at 6% is 4.4651. What gain should Seller-Lessee Corp. recognize, and at what amount should it record the right-of-use asset?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gain of $900,000; right-of-use asset of $1,116,275

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gain of $900,000; right-of-use asset of $781,393

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gain of $565,118; right-of-use asset of $1,116,275

choices.label: D
choices.text: No gain is recognized at the transfer date; the $900,000 is deferred and amortized over the 5-year leaseback term; right-of-use asset of $1,116,275

questions.explanation: When a sale-leaseback qualifies as a sale and is executed at fair value, the seller-lessee recognizes the entire gain immediately: $3,000,000 - $2,100,000 = $900,000. The leaseback is then accounted for as an ordinary lease, so the right-of-use asset is measured at the present value of the leaseback payments, $250,000 x 4.4651 = $1,116,275, with an equal lease liability. The $781,393 figure measures the right-of-use asset as a retained proportion of the old carrying amount, and the $565,118 gain recognizes only the portion of the gain relating to the rights transferred to the buyer; both reflect the proportionate approach that U.S. GAAP does not use. Deferring the entire gain and amortizing it over the leaseback term was the superseded practice under prior lease guidance and is no longer permitted.
questions.explanationJa: セール&リースバックが売却の要件を満たし、公正価値で実行された場合、売主借手は利得の全額を即時に認識する。すなわち $3,000,000 − $2,100,000 = $900,000 である。リースバックはその後、通常のリースとして処理されるため、使用権資産はリースバック料の現在価値 $250,000 × 4.4651 = $1,116,275 で測定し、同額のリース負債を計上する。$781,393 は使用権資産を従来の帳簿価額のうち保持した割合として測定したものであり、$565,118 の利得は買主に移転した権利に対応する部分のみを認識したものである。いずれも米国基準が採用していない比例配分アプローチによるものである。利得全額を繰り延べてリースバック期間にわたり償却する処理は、旧リース基準下の実務であり現在は認められない。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — Year 1 Effect on Pretax Income
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Seller-Lessee Corp. sells equipment with a carrying amount of $400,000 to Buyer-Lessor Corp. for $520,000 cash, which equals the equipment's fair value. Seller-Lessee Corp. immediately leases the equipment back for 4 years at $60,000 per year payable at the end of each year. The transfer qualifies as a sale under ASC 606 and the leaseback is classified as an operating lease. Seller-Lessee Corp. incurred no initial direct costs. What is the net effect of this transaction on Seller-Lessee Corp.'s Year 1 pretax income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $120,000 increase

choices.label: B
choices.text: $60,000 decrease

choices.label: C
choices.text: $60,000 increase

choices.label: D
choices.text: $30,000 decrease

questions.explanation: Two items hit Year 1 income. The sale qualifies and is at fair value, so the full gain of $520,000 - $400,000 = $120,000 is recognized at the transfer date. The operating leaseback produces a single straight-line lease cost equal to total lease payments divided by the lease term, or $240,000 / 4 = $60,000 for Year 1. The net effect is a $120,000 - $60,000 = $60,000 increase. The $120,000 increase counts the gain but omits the lease cost that begins running immediately. The $60,000 decrease reflects the lease cost while denying any gain, which would be the result only if the transfer failed to qualify as a sale. The $30,000 decrease amortizes the gain over the 4-year leaseback at $30,000 per year against $60,000 of lease cost, which applies the superseded deferred-gain approach.
questions.explanationJa: Year 1 の損益には2項目が影響する。売却は要件を満たし公正価値で行われているため、利得の全額 $520,000 − $400,000 = $120,000 を移転日に認識する。オペレーティングのリースバックからは、総リース料をリース期間で除した定額のリース費用、すなわち Year 1 は $240,000 ÷ 4 = $60,000 が生じる。正味の影響は $120,000 − $60,000 = $60,000 の増加となる。$120,000 の増加は利得のみを数え、直ちに発生し始めるリース費用を除外している。$60,000 の減少はリース費用を反映しつつ利得を一切認めないもので、移転が売却要件を満たさない場合にのみ生じる結果である。$30,000 の減少は利得を4年のリースバック期間にわたり年 $30,000 で償却し $60,000 のリース費用と相殺したもので、廃止された繰延利益アプローチを適用している。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — Repurchase Option Exception
questions.stem: Seller-Lessee Corp. transfers a standard model of construction equipment to Buyer-Lessor Corp. and leases it back for 3 years. The equipment has a remaining economic life of 15 years. The contract gives Seller-Lessee Corp. an option to repurchase the equipment at the end of the leaseback at its then-fair value, and equipment substantially the same as the transferred equipment is readily available in the marketplace. The leaseback is classified as an operating lease. How should the transfer be accounted for?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a financing, because the existence of any repurchase option means the seller-lessee retains control of the asset

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a financing, because the repurchase option is substantive and is expected to be exercised

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a sale only if the repurchase option price is fixed at an amount below the expected fair value

choices.label: D
choices.text: As a sale, because the option price is the fair value at the exercise date and substantially the same assets are readily available in the marketplace

questions.explanation: A repurchase option ordinarily prevents a transfer from qualifying as a sale, but there is a narrow exception: the option does not preclude sale accounting if the exercise price is the fair value of the asset at the date of exercise and assets substantially the same as the transferred asset are readily available in the marketplace. Both conditions are satisfied here, and the leaseback is not a finance lease, so the transfer is a sale. Treating any repurchase option as fatal overlooks that exception. Whether the option is expected to be exercised is not the test under this exception. An option priced below expected fair value would push the conclusion the other way, because a bargain repurchase price is precisely the kind of term that shows control was never transferred.
questions.explanationJa: 買戻選択権は通常、移転が売却として認められることを妨げるが、狭い例外がある。行使価格が行使日における資産の公正価値であり、移転資産と実質的に同一の資産が市場で容易に入手できる場合、当該選択権は売却処理を妨げない。本問は両要件を満たし、リースバックもファイナンス・リースではないため、移転は売却となる。買戻選択権があれば一律に売却を否定するのは、この例外を見落としている。行使が見込まれるかどうかは、この例外における判定基準ではない。予想公正価値を下回る価格の選択権はむしろ逆の結論を導く。割安な買戻価格こそ、支配が移転していないことを示す典型的な条件だからである。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — Finance Leaseback Defeats the Sale
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Seller-Lessee Corp. sells a specialized machine with a carrying amount of $700,000 to Buyer-Lessor Corp. for $960,000 cash, which equals the machine's fair value. The machine has a remaining economic life of 12 years, and Seller-Lessee Corp. leases it back for 11 years. There is no repurchase option. What amount of gain should Seller-Lessee Corp. recognize on the transfer at January 1, Year 1?

choices.label: D
choices.text: $260,000, recognized as a reduction of the right-of-use asset rather than in income

questions.explanation: The leaseback covers 11 of the machine's 12 remaining years of economic life, which is 91.7% and therefore a major part of that life, so the leaseback is a finance lease to Seller-Lessee Corp. When the leaseback would be a finance lease, the transfer does not qualify as a sale no matter how the price compares with fair value. Seller-Lessee Corp. keeps the machine on its balance sheet, records the $960,000 as a financial liability, and recognizes no gain. The $260,000 amount is the gain that would arise if the transfer had qualified as a sale. The $23,636 amount spreads that gain over the 11-year leaseback. Reducing a right-of-use asset by the gain is not an option here, because no right-of-use asset is recognized in a failed sale-leaseback.
questions.explanationJa: リースバックは機械の残存経済的耐用年数12年のうち11年、すなわち91.7%を占め、耐用年数の主要部分に当たるため、売主借手にとってファイナンス・リースとなる。リースバックがファイナンス・リースとなる場合、売却価格が公正価値とどう比較されるかにかかわらず、移転は売却の要件を満たさない。売主借手は機械を貸借対照表に残したまま $960,000 を金融負債として計上し、利得は認識しない。$260,000 は移転が売却要件を満たした場合に生じる利得である。$23,636 はその利得を11年のリースバック期間に配分したものである。利得を使用権資産から減額する選択肢も成り立たない。売却要件を満たさないセール&リースバックでは使用権資産を認識しないからである。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — Seller-Lessee Journal Entry
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Seller-Lessee Corp. sells a building with a carrying amount of $600,000 to Buyer-Lessor Corp. for $1,000,000 cash, which equals the building's fair value. Seller-Lessee Corp. leases the building back for 6 years under a leaseback classified as an operating lease. The present value of the leaseback payments, discounted at the appropriate rate, is $450,000. The transfer qualifies as a sale under ASC 606. Which of the following describes the entry Seller-Lessee Corp. records on January 1, Year 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Debit cash $1,000,000 and right-of-use asset $450,000; credit building $600,000, lease liability $450,000, and deferred gain $400,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: Debit cash $1,000,000 and right-of-use asset $450,000; credit building $600,000, lease liability $450,000, and gain on sale $400,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: Debit cash $1,000,000; credit building $600,000 and gain on sale $400,000, with no right-of-use asset or lease liability recognized because the leaseback is an operating lease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Debit cash $1,000,000; credit financial liability $1,000,000, with the building remaining on Seller-Lessee Corp.'s books

questions.explanation: Because the transfer qualifies as a sale at fair value, Seller-Lessee Corp. derecognizes the building at its $600,000 carrying amount, records the $1,000,000 of cash, and recognizes the full $400,000 gain in income immediately. It then accounts for the leaseback like any other lease, recording a right-of-use asset and lease liability of $450,000. Crediting a deferred gain instead of income applies the superseded approach that spread the gain over the leaseback term. Omitting the right-of-use asset and lease liability is wrong because an operating lease is still recognized on the balance sheet under ASC 842. Recording the proceeds as a financial liability with the building retained is the accounting for a transfer that fails to qualify as a sale.
questions.explanationJa: 移転が公正価値による売却の要件を満たすため、売主借手は建物を帳簿価額 $600,000 で認識中止し、現金 $1,000,000 を計上し、$400,000 の利得全額を直ちに損益として認識する。その後リースバックは他のリースと同様に処理し、$450,000 の使用権資産とリース負債を計上する。損益ではなく繰延利益に貸記するのは、利得をリースバック期間に配分していた廃止済みのアプローチである。使用権資産とリース負債を計上しないのは誤りで、ASC 842 ではオペレーティング・リースも貸借対照表に認識する。受領額を金融負債として計上し建物を残すのは、売却要件を満たさない移転に対する処理である。

questions.subtopic: Failed Sale-Leaseback — Year 1 Total Expense
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Seller-Lessee Corp. transfers equipment with a carrying amount of $900,000 and a remaining useful life of 10 years with no salvage value to Buyer-Lessor Corp. for $1,200,000 cash and leases it back. The transfer does not qualify as a sale under ASC 606. The leaseback requires annual payments of $150,000 due at the end of each year, and the imputed interest rate on the financing is 8%. Seller-Lessee Corp. depreciates equipment on a straight-line basis. What total amount of expense should Seller-Lessee Corp. recognize in Year 1 in connection with this transaction?
questions.explanation: In a failed sale-leaseback the equipment is never derecognized, so Seller-Lessee Corp. continues to depreciate it on its existing basis: $900,000 / 10 = $90,000 for Year 1. The $1,200,000 received is a financial liability, and Year 1 interest expense is $1,200,000 x 8% = $96,000. Total Year 1 expense is $90,000 + $96,000 = $186,000. The $150,000 amount treats the annual payment as rent expense, which is what would be recorded if the arrangement were a true operating leaseback. The $96,000 amount recognizes interest but forgets that the asset remains on the books and must still be depreciated. The $216,000 amount depreciates the equipment on the $1,200,000 transfer price, but a failed sale provides no step-up in basis.
questions.explanationJa: 売却要件を満たさないセール&リースバックでは設備の認識中止を行わないため、売主借手は従来の帳簿価額に基づき減価償却を継続する。Year 1 は $900,000 ÷ 10 = $90,000 である。受領した $1,200,000 は金融負債であり、Year 1 の支払利息は $1,200,000 × 8% = $96,000。Year 1 の費用合計は $90,000 + $96,000 = $186,000 となる。$150,000 は年間支払額を賃借料費用として扱ったもので、真のオペレーティング・リースバックであった場合の処理である。$96,000 は利息を認識しているが、資産が帳簿に残り減価償却を要する点を失念している。$216,000 は移転価格 $1,200,000 に基づき減価償却しているが、売却要件を満たさない移転では取得原価の付け替えは生じない。

questions.subtopic: Sale-Leaseback — Buyer-Lessor in a Qualifying Sale
questions.stem: In a sale-leaseback transaction in which the transfer qualifies as a sale under ASC 606, how does the buyer-lessor account for the transaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It recognizes a note receivable for the amount paid and recognizes interest income over the leaseback term, without recognizing the underlying asset.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It recognizes the underlying asset at the seller-lessee's carrying amount and recognizes any excess paid as a loss.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It recognizes the purchase of the underlying asset and classifies the leaseback as a sales-type lease.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It recognizes the purchase of the underlying asset under other applicable GAAP and accounts for the leaseback under the lessor model, classifying it as an operating or a direct financing lease.

questions.explanation: When the transfer qualifies as a sale, the buyer-lessor accounts for the purchase under the GAAP that would apply to any other acquisition of that asset, and then applies the ordinary lessor model to the leaseback. The leaseback cannot be a sales-type lease, because a leaseback that the buyer-lessor would classify as sales-type is itself a condition that causes the transfer to fail as a sale, so the only classifications available are operating and direct financing. Recognizing a note receivable without the asset is the accounting for a failed sale-leaseback. Measuring the asset at the seller-lessee's carrying amount and recording a loss for the difference has no support; the buyer-lessor records the asset at the consideration it paid.
questions.explanationJa: 移転が売却の要件を満たす場合、買主貸手は当該資産の取得に通常適用される会計基準に従って購入を処理し、リースバックには通常の貸手モデルを適用する。リースバックが販売型リースとなることはあり得ない。買主貸手が販売型に分類するようなリースバックは、それ自体が移転を売却として認めない要件だからである。したがって分類はオペレーティングまたは直接金融型に限られる。資産を認識せず債権のみを計上するのは、売却要件を満たさないセール&リースバックに対する処理である。資産を売主借手の帳簿価額で測定し差額を損失とする扱いには根拠がなく、買主貸手は支払った対価で資産を計上する。

questions.subtopic: Failed Sale-Leaseback — Statement of Cash Flows
questions.stem: Seller-Lessee Corp. received $2,000,000 of cash from Buyer-Lessor Corp. in a sale-leaseback transaction in which the transfer of the asset did not qualify as a sale under ASC 606. How should Seller-Lessee Corp. classify the $2,000,000 of cash received in its statement of cash flows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a financing activity inflow

questions.explanation: Because the transfer failed to qualify as a sale, the cash received is the proceeds of a borrowing rather than the proceeds of selling an asset, and proceeds from borrowings are financing activities. The asset stays on the balance sheet and the subsequent payments are split between interest and principal reduction. Reporting the cash as an investing inflow would be right only if an asset had actually been sold and derecognized. Operating classification does not fit, because nothing about the transaction represents revenue from the entity's ongoing operations. Splitting the proceeds between investing and operating based on the carrying amount has no support in the cash flow guidance, which classifies the entire inflow according to the nature of the transaction.
questions.explanationJa: 移転が売却の要件を満たさないため、受領した現金は資産売却の収入ではなく借入による収入であり、借入収入は財務活動に分類される。資産は貸借対照表に残り、その後の支払は利息部分と元本返済部分に配分される。投資活動の収入として報告するのは、実際に資産が売却され認識中止された場合にのみ正しい。営業活動への分類も適合しない。本取引には企業の継続的な営業活動からの収益に当たる要素がないからである。帳簿価額を基準に収入を投資活動と営業活動に分割する処理はキャッシュ・フロー基準に根拠がなく、収入全額を取引の性質に応じて分類する。

questions.subtopic: Failed Sale-Leaseback — Subsequent Qualification as a Sale
questions.stem: Seller-Lessee Corp.'s transfer of a building to Buyer-Lessor Corp. on January 1, Year 1 did not qualify as a sale because Seller-Lessee Corp. held a substantive option to repurchase the building at a fixed price. The building has remained on Seller-Lessee Corp.'s books and the cash received has been accounted for as a financial liability. On December 31, Year 4, the repurchase option expires unexercised, and at that date control of the building transfers to Buyer-Lessor Corp. How should Seller-Lessee Corp. account for the expiration of the option?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continue to account for the transaction as a financing until the leaseback term ends, at which point the building and the liability are removed with no gain or loss.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recognize the gain retrospectively as of January 1, Year 1 by restating the prior periods, because the transaction has now been shown to be a sale.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Derecognize the building and the remaining financial liability at December 31, Year 4 and recognize the resulting gain or loss at that date.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recognize no gain or loss at any date, because the amount of any gain was fixed at the original transfer date and is never recognized in a failed sale-leaseback.

questions.explanation: A failed sale-leaseback is reassessed, and the sale is recognized when the transaction subsequently satisfies the requirements for a sale, which happens here when the repurchase option expires and control passes. At that date Seller-Lessee Corp. removes the building's carrying amount and the remaining financial liability from its balance sheet and recognizes the difference as a gain or loss, and it begins accounting for the remaining leaseback under the lessee model. Waiting until the leaseback term ends delays recognition past the date control actually transferred. Restating prior periods is wrong because the transfer genuinely was not a sale in those periods; this is a new event, not an error. Saying no gain is ever recognized confuses deferral with permanent non-recognition.
questions.explanationJa: 売却要件を満たさなかったセール&リースバックは再評価され、取引が事後的に売却の要件を満たした時点で売却を認識する。本問では買戻選択権が失効し支配が移転した時点がこれに当たる。その日に売主借手は建物の帳簿価額と残存する金融負債を貸借対照表から除去し、差額を利得または損失として認識するとともに、残りのリースバックを借手モデルで処理し始める。リースバック期間の終了まで待つのは、支配が実際に移転した日より認識を遅らせることになる。過年度の修正再表示は誤りである。当該期間において移転は実際に売却ではなかったのであり、これは誤謬ではなく新たな事象だからである。利得を一切認識しないという考え方は、繰延べと恒久的な非認識を混同している。
